title: Yellow Vests and unions march in Paris against cost of living
seoTitle: Paris march against cost of living

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against the high cost of living, stagnant wages, and the destruction of public services.
tea.want: Participants demand higher wages, affordable housing, and fairer taxation.
tea.changed: Nov 21: Protesters gathered at Place de la République in Paris for a march toward Place de la Nation.

summary: On November 21, 2026, trade unions, youth groups, and the Yellow Vests movement held a nationwide day of protest in France, marking the sixth consecutive Saturday of demonstrations against the rising cost of living. In Paris, protesters gathered at Place de la République for a march to Place de la Nation. The event coincides with the eighth anniversary of the Yellow Vests movement. Organisers include the inter-union collective of Île-de-France, comprising the CGT, CFDT, FO, FSU, and Solidaires, alongside youth organisations and the Droit au logement association. Authorities deployed 70,000 police and gendarmes across the country to monitor the demonstrations. In Paris, the police implemented security measures, including the closure of several metro stations, to manage the crowds.
response: Interior Minister Laurent Nunez announced the deployment of 70,000 police and gendarmes nationwide to monitor the protests. In Paris, authorities implemented security measures including public transport disruptions, while in Lyon, protests were banned in the city center.

crowd.text: Around 400 people gathered at Place de la Republique in central Paris, according to Le Parisien.

updates.text: Interior Minister Laurent Nunez announced 70,000 police and gendarmes would be deployed nationwide for the protests.
Protesters gathered at Place de la République in Paris ahead of a scheduled march to Place de la Nation.
